- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1-2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.27) and forecast is falling, increase forecast by 1-2% to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Overshoots after spikes (forecast > true by 3%+ in 3-5 days) should be capped at 2% above recent 7-day average.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5%+ above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1-1.5% per day until convergence.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle; reduce first 5-7 days by 1-1.5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, forecast should be 1-2% below the 18-day moving average for next 3-5 days.
